# Psalm 38 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A)

---

**1** A-psalm of-David. For-a-memorial.

**2** YHWH, do-not in-Your-anger rebuke-me, and-in-Your-wrath do-not discipline-me.

**3** For Your-arrows have-sunk into-me, and-Your-hand has-come-down upon-me.

**4** There-is-no soundness in-my-flesh because-of Your-indignation; there-is-no health in-my-bones because-of my-sin.

**5** For my-iniquities have-gone over my-head; like-a-heavy burden they-are-too-heavy for-me.

**6** My-wounds stink and-fester because-of my-foolishness.

**7** I-am-bowed-down; I-am-brought-very-low; all the-day I-go-about mourning.

**8** For my-loins are-filled with-burning, and-there-is-no soundness in-my-flesh.

**9** I-am-feeble and-crushed utterly; I-groan because-of the-turmoil of-my-heart.

**10** Lord, before-You [is] all my-desire, and-my-groaning from-You is-not hidden.

**11** My-heart pounds; my-strength fails-me, and-the-light of-my-eyes — even-it [is] not with-me.

**12** My-loved-ones and-my-friends stand-away from-my-affliction, and-my-neighbors stand at-a-distance.

**13** And-those-seeking my-life lay-snares, and-those-seeking my-harm speak destruction, and-treacheries all the-day they-mutter.

**14** But-I, like-a-deaf-man, do-not hear; and-like-a-mute who does-not open his-mouth.

**15** And-I-am like-a-man who does-not hear, and-in-whose mouth [are] no-arguments.

**16** For in-You, YHWH, I-hope; You will-answer, Lord my-God.

**17** For I-said, 'Lest they-rejoice over-me; when-my-foot slips, against-me they-magnify [themselves].'

**18** For I [am] ready to-stumble, and-my-pain [is] before-me continually.

**19** For my-iniquity I-confess; I-am-anxious because-of my-sin.

**20** But-my-enemies are-vigorous [and] strong, and-many [are] those-hating-me falsely.

**21** And-those-repaying evil for good oppose-me because I-pursue good.

**22** Do-not forsake-me, YHWH; my-God, do-not be-far from-me.

---
## EMET Literal Notes

- **38:4-5**: Sin is described as both wound and weight — it festers in the body and crushes the spirit. The psalm refuses to separate physical and moral suffering.

— EMET
